category_title: Students with IDD in Task Learning Classes (SAT) focused on autonomy and adult life skills
student_description: This student struggles with the transition to secondary education and experiences anxiety and friction during unplanned social interactions with peers from ordinary classes. They uniquely require highly structured environments, specifically step-by-step instructions with concrete examples followed by scheduled decompression time, as well as meticulously planned peer support rather than organic socialization.

criteria.rationale: This student requires academic content and tasks to be broken down sequentially and grounded in clear examples to ensure comprehension.
criteria.check: The tutor breaks the immediate task or concept into sequential steps and provides at least one concrete example to illustrate the expectation.

criteria.rationale: The student needs the assurance of scheduled free time to play and relax after completing step-by-step tasks to maintain satisfaction and task completion.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly establishes that completing the current task or steps will be followed by a designated period of free time to relax or play.

criteria.rationale: The student experiences anxiety and conflict when forced into unstructured social situations with ordinary class peers.
criteria.check: The tutor provides a specific, structured entry point or role for peer interaction, explicitly avoiding instructing the student to simply 'join' or mingle with the group organically.
